clue.text: Religious rebel showing a refusal to accept suggestion

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
an informal word of refusal
a tip is a helpful suggestion

explanation.surface: A dissident in the church is stubbornly refusing to take advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing a refusal' tempts you to take ANTI as the refusal; the refusal is the informal no-word, which swallows the suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: An antipope is a rival claimant set up against the lawfully elected head of the Catholic Church, so a rebel within religion.

clue.text: Unexpected power in a classification of wine

indicators.note: something placed in another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
brut is the label for very dry sparkling wine
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find strength listed among the grades of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: P sits inside BRUT, with A in front. Brut is the driest standard grade on a champagne label.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt change is sudden and without warning, so it comes as a surprise; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: A lot of birdsong around close part of plant

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
to be around something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a trill is a warbling birdsong, cut short here
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: Birds are singing loudly around a nearby bit of greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like an adjective meaning near, but it is the noun, the close of something, its finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the thin coiling shoot a climbing plant uses to grip supports, so it is one part of the plant.

clue.text: Favouring Christian philosopher’s prediction

blocks.note: to be pro something is to favour it
the Gnostics were early Christian thinkers who prized secret knowledge

explanation.surface: A philosopher who is keen on Christianity makes a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognostic is a sign or forecast of what is to come, used as a noun much like omen or forecast.

clue.text: Mean-spirited American blocking medicine, hatred swamping love

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so one piece lodges within another
to swamp something is to engulf it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: US is the standard abbreviation for American
a pill is a dose of medicine
animus is hostility or ill will
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A petty American is getting in the way of treatment, his hatred overwhelming any affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two separate containers side by side, the first half then the second; love as O comes from the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Pusillanimous means timid and lacking courage, literally small-souled, which overlaps with being petty and mean of spirit.

clue.text: Papa recalled row about opening of clothes drawer

indicators.note: a thing recalled is called back, so it runs in the backward direction
to be about something is to be placed around it
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a row is a line
first letter of clothes

explanation.surface: Dad remembers an argument over a chest of drawers full of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes drawer' suggests furniture, but a drawer is also one who draws. LINE turns round to ENIL and takes C inside, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is the tool an artist sketches with, so it is a drawer in the sense of something that makes drawings.

clue.text: Simple question to get out of rough?

indicators.note: something told to get out of a place leaves it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question
feeling rough means feeling sick or nauseous

explanation.surface: A golfer asks a plain question about escaping the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' suggests the golf course, but here it means feeling unwell, QUEASY; removing QU leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and easy are synonyms describing a task that needs little effort or skill.

clue.text: Islands stocking dyestuff for Indian city

indicators.note: a shop stocking goods holds them inside, so one piece contains another

blocks.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
henna is a reddish dye made from a plant

explanation.surface: Some islands keep a supply of dye destined for a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off the French coast and belong to the British Crown; their abbreviation CI wraps round the dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Chennai, formerly Madras, is the capital of Tamil Nadu on the southeast coast of India.

clue.text: Greatly upset about husband’s aversion to any action?

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
to be about something is to be placed around it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone is very annoyed at her husband's refusal to do anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: GREATLY is both the fodder and, on the surface, an adverb for 'upset'. Its rearrangement goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is sluggishness and lack of energy, which the question mark playfully casts as a dislike of doing anything.

clue.text: Collapse after losing one marathon?

indicators.note: what remains after losing something has had it taken away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to collapse or fall apart is to go to ruin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An athlete collapses after missing out in a long-distance race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: a marathon is one kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long race on foot, one particular instance of a running event.

clue.text: Unpleasant odour circulating? Only odour is on the way out

indicators.note: something circulating goes round, so the letters turn back on themselves

blocks.note: BO is body odour
sole means only
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A nasty smell is drifting about, and the only smell around is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'odour' tempts a solver to look for one word twice; the first is BO, the second SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolescent describes something passing out of use and becoming outdated, not yet gone but on its way.

clue.text: “Delicately flavoured” identified as description for dips?

blocks.note: a light dish is delicately flavoured
to finger a suspect is to identify them

explanation.surface: A food writer labels a set of party dips as subtly flavoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dips' looks like the food served with crisps; in slang a dip is a pickpocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-fingered means skilled at stealing, so it is how one would characterise pickpockets.

clue.text: A bumpy approach to one’s way of thinking?

definitions.text: A bumpy approach to one’s way of thinking?

blocks.clueFragment: A bumpy approach to one’s way of thinking?
blocks.note: surface reading: an uneven or rocky road towards understanding someone's views

blocks.clueFragment: A bumpy approach to one’s way of thinking?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a discredited science that read character and mind from the lumps on a skull

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bumpy' seems to mean rough going, but it is literal: the bumps are on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This Victorian pseudoscience claimed that the shape and bumps of a skull revealed mental faculties and character.

clue.text: Popular account brought back ancient language

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
AC is an abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A well-loved story has revived a dead tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: IN for popular is a crossword staple; AC is the bookkeeping abbreviation for account, turned round to CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inca is used loosely for Quechua, the tongue spoken in the old Peruvian empire of that name.

clue.text: Fielders leading colleagues restricting runs in follow-on?

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: the slips are close catching positions beside the wicketkeeper in cricket
colleagues together form a team
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders ahead of their teammates hold down the scoring when the other side has to bat again.
explanation.walkthrough: A follow-on in cricket is when a side far behind must bat again at once; here it means whatever trails behind something. R goes inside TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipstream is the current of air behind a moving vehicle, or figuratively the wake a following thing travels in.

clue.text: Old man and old woman receiving large then small quantity of blood

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An elderly couple are given a big then a little amount of blood in a transfusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small quantity' wants to run together, but 'small' is just the size letter; 'quantity of blood' is the definition. The large letter goes inside the father, the small one between the parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale liquid component of blood in which the cells are suspended, so a portion of the blood.

clue.text: Impressive archer getting middle of rings

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, with the ends cut away

blocks.note: William Tell was the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head
the central three letters of rings

explanation.surface: A skilled bowman is hitting the centre of the target's rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of rings' suggests the bullseye of an archery target, which neatly suits the archer.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling argument or blow is striking and effective, so it makes a strong impression.

clue.text: Studies I should leave US institute to conduct

indicators.note: whatever leaves is no longer present, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: one who trains studies for a qualification
taken as written, the letter to remove
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A student decides to quit an American university to go off and lead an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conduct' tempts towards leading an orchestra; here it is the physics sense of carrying heat or electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire that conducts electricity passes it along, which is to transmit it; the verbs are synonyms in physics.

clue.text: Composer put out missing opening in capital of Italy

indicators.note: a word missing its opening has lost its first letter
the capital of a word is its first, capital letter

blocks.note: put out means annoyed, or cross, here without its first letter
taken as written
first letter of Italy

explanation.surface: A composer is upset to be left out of the opening night in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Italy' cries out for Rome, but it means only the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote The Barber of Seville and William Tell, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Answer fits awkwardly into speech

indicators.note: done awkwardly means done clumsily, out of order, so the letters are rearranged
something put into another thing goes inside it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
one's say is one's spoken contribution

explanation.surface: A reply squeezes clumsily into somebody's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, as in to answer a need.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer a requirement or demand is to meet it fully, the same as to satisfy it.

clue.text: I’m quiet — is he primarily mischievous?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
taken as written
first letter of he

explanation.surface: A child stays silent, prompting the question of whether he is mainly up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano, the soft dynamic marking in music; the dash and question mark are just surface punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish describes a playful, naughty streak like that of a little imp, a close synonym of mischievous.

clue.text: Expensive policy not popular for part of church

indicators.note: not having something means it is absent, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a steep price is a high one
a party line is its policy
what is in is popular

explanation.surface: A costly insurance policy that nobody likes is taken out to cover part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policy' suggests insurance, but it means a line, as in the party line; removing IN leaves LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall tower and spire rising above a church, so one section of the building.

clue.text: Operatic heroine is historic, not new

indicators.note: not having something means it is absent, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
olden means belonging to times long past
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A singer's leading role is a classic, not a fresh creation.
explanation.walkthrough: OLDEN loses its N, leaving the mock-archaic spelling OLDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess who loves Tristan in Wagner's opera, its leading female role.

clue.text: A, B, C, D, F or G?

definitions.text: A, B, C, D, F or G?

blocks.clueFragment: A, B, C, D, F or G
blocks.note: the run from A to G with its fifth letter left out; every item is also a pitch name in music

explanation.surface: A quiz asks which letters from a school report card a pupil might get.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: each letter names a musical pitch, and the list leaves out E, so the answer reads NOT E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Western music the seven pitch names run from A to G, and each of those letters names a musical tone.

clue.text: Vocalist in boy group’s initial worry

indicators.note: an initial is a word's first letter

blocks.note: a son is a boy child
first letter of group
stress is anxiety or worry

explanation.surface: A singer in a boy band is fretting at the start of their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container indicator, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A songstress is a female singer, so a vocalist; the word is a slightly old-fashioned feminine form.

clue.text: Prepare celebration for old-fashioned person

blocks.note: to do a meal or room is to prepare it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone throws a party for a fuddy-duddy relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' as a noun for a party is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct bird gave its name to anyone hopelessly behind the times, as in the phrase dead as a dodo.

clue.text: Fail to understand consumerist in action

indicators.note: letters in action are moving about, so they rearrange themselves

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Watching a shopaholic at work, an observer cannot make sense of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In action' reads as watching the shopper at work, but it tells you to set the letters moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To misconstrue is to interpret wrongly, so to get the wrong idea and not grasp the real meaning.

clue.text: Apostle lacking universal example of friendship

indicators.note: something lacking a part is without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: St Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A disciple without wide appeal still offers a model of companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is a friend, so an instance or embodiment of friendship; the definition is loose rather than a strict synonym.

clue.text: One entertaining the mature trifle? Wow!

blocks.note: to trifle with something is to toy with it, and a trifle is a toy
'Boy!' is an exclamation of surprise, like wow

explanation.surface: A host serves a pudding to the grown-ups, and they are thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' suggests the British layered dessert of sponge, custard and cream; here it means a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy boy is a young man in a relationship with a much older woman, so he entertains a mature partner.

clue.text: Mother leading plot in a European novel

indicators.note: something placed in another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a garden plot is a bed
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A mother takes charge of the storyline in a book written by someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' only sets the order, mother before plot; both then sit between the article and the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is the 1859 first full-length novel by George Eliot, set among farmers and craftsmen of rural England.
